text:
Maya: Heads-up — ran the nightly quant bake with FP8 and GPTQ variants against the table/format evals and seeing a weird spike in structured-output hallucinations for FP8 only. baseline (fp16) BLEU=42.1, fp8 BLEU=37.9, gptq-int8 BLEU=41.8. hallucination rate (schema breaks) +4.2% for fp8.
Jordan: ugh. can you paste an example where output loses JSON keys or invents fields?
Maya: sure, sample from failing shard:
```
input: convert table to json
expected: {"rows": [{"id": 1, "name": "A"}, ...]}
fp16: {"rows": [{"id": 1, "name": "A"}]}
fp8: {"rows": [{"id": 1, "name": "A"}], "summary": "generated 2 rows"} <-- extra invented summary
gptq: {"rows": [{"id": 1, "name": "A"}]}
```
Maya: the extra `summary` field is exactly what we flagged; also some numeric tokens get reformatted (e.g., `00123` -> `123`).
Sam: interesting — could be seed/ordering of quantization or compilation kernel nondeterminism. did you rerun with deterministic seed and single-threaded? also which runtime and kernel set?
Maya: ran on dev-runtime v2.4 (our fp8 kernels) with `RUNTIME_THREADS=8`. not deterministic. when forced `OMP_NUM_THREADS=1` and seed pinned, the rate drops to +1.1% but still > baseline.
Esther: any difference in request profile (max_seq/batch)? maybe batch boundary triggers KV prefix loss.
Maya: test config: `batch_size=4, max_tokens=512, prefix_cache=true`. suspect boundary with prefix length ~128.
Jordan: can you bisect model commit vs compiler flags? sometimes fp8 codegen had a micro-change. also compare `quant_scale` clipping.
Maya: starting bisect: running 4 commits across bringup window. started at 2115004400. will post results.
deploy-bot: deploy triggered: quant-bisect-job-2115004321 -> running commit_range 0af3..d2b6
Liam: also try re-running the failing prompts with AWQ-int8 profile — AWQ had different per-channel scaling and sometimes fixes stray token generation.
Maya: ran AWQ quick check: AWQ-int8 BLEU=40.7, hallucination +0.9% -> much better than FP8 but slightly worse BLEU than fp16.
Sam: so possibilities: fp8 per-channel scale or kernel fusion bug causing non-linear rounding on prefix tokens. If deterministic run reduced but didn't eliminate, maybe accumulation precision in KV cache.
Esther: can you dump KV cache token ids for fp8 vs fp16 at the boundary? even a 1-token shift would cascade.
Maya: yes, attached sample KV diffs (pasted below):
```
fp16_kv_ids: [1203, 1204, 1205, 1206]
fp8_kv_ids:  [1203, 1204, 1206, 1207]  // missing 1205, shifted
```
Maya: that exact shift maps to where JSON keys start; when tokens misaligned, model invents `summary` because it attends to wrong prefix.
Jordan: ok that's actionable — root cause likely KV eviction or pack boundary bug in fp8 continuous-batching path. escalate to runtime team.
Sam: add reproducer that toggles `prefix_cache` and `batch_size` (1..8) and seeds. Also run an instrumented kernel with bounds checks on KV write.
Maya: creating issue: https://redwood.internal/issue/ML-quant/2115004321 (proto). adding logs and failing input shard.
Esther: quick mitigation: add a routing rule that sends table/format routes to AWQ-int8 or fp16 for now until fix. Can we do that via config flag per-deployment?
Liam: yes — `deployment->route_rules` supports model-family fallback. I'll add a canary rule for customers in dedicated pools.
Maya: thanks. I'll finish bisect and attach kernel-level dump. planning to run full eval with `OMP_NUM_THREADS=1` and `BATCH=1..8` sweep overnight.
Jordan: great. ping once you have the narrow commit or repro snippet. :thumbsup:
Maya: will do — adding summary to issue and closing loop here once root commit found.
deploy-bot: job quant-bisect-job-2115004321 completed: suspect commit d2b6a4 -> runtime/kernel fusion for fp8 write-path. (queued follow-up review)
Maya: confirmed d2b6a4 reproduces locally with minimal repro. opening PR to revert micro-optimization and adding unit test for kv-aliasing.
Sam: nice catch. after PR lands, run the same nightly to confirm metrics recover to within noise.
Maya: noted. final numbers after patch on staging: fp8 BLEU=41.9, hallucination +0.6% (within tolerances). rolling patch to canary.
Esther: perfect. moving route rule to prefer AWQ only for 2h while canary finishes. :white_check_mark:
Liam: we'll add a postmortem note in the quant playbook about KV-indexing and batch boundaries.
Maya: thanks everyone. saved the failing prompt set to `/evals/outputs/2115004321/failing_prompts.json`
